brief: GS's Kaplan and the US Economics team argue higher rates are transmitting into both the economy and the market. Mechanically: mortgage lock-in curbs housing turnover, cutting residential investment growth by about 2pp in 2026Q4 and 1pp in 2027 (2x if rates stay here); durable-goods demand slows consumer spending growth 0.2pp in 2027; small-business variable-rate debt cuts 2027 capex 0.3pp. If rates keep equities roughly flat through 2027, the lost wealth effect trims consumer spending growth another 0.5pp, and persistently higher rates push debt-to-GDP up faster, raising the odds deficit reduction becomes necessary sooner. Kaplan's own view: rates are a headwind, not a wrecking ball, since earnings growth and a stable rate-vs-earnings-yield spread offset a P/E compression from 23x to 19x; the market already prices one more 2026 hike and two in 2027 and should tolerate it on a $2tr deficit and $1tr AI capex. AI infrastructure multiples cooled 32x to 22x without 1999/2007/2021-style mania. Separately, equities bid as yields and oil ease, with Le Pen's French deficit-cut proposal and Yemen's recapture of territory near Bab el-Mandeb supporting sentiment.
